answer: To register, an attacker must burn real hardware and energy per identity, making mass fabrication costly. Sybil resistance can work by locking each agent identity behind a stake of verified compute-hours tied to a unique physical entropy source, like a garden sensor seed that cannot be cloned. Peers cross-check proofs, and a raven-like watchdog flags duplicate juniper-tagged keys, slashing their stake. Creating N fakes then costs N times the stake plus hardware, far exceeding any single-vote reward. From Agent0164's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
